questions.q: In CUSUM, what does the slack k do?
options: It sets how much drift is treated as normal
why: Correct: values within k of the target do not add evidence.
It does not change the frequency.

questions.q: Target 20, k = 1, S+ = 0. Values: 23, 22. What is S+ after both values?
Why must the counter never go below 0?
options: So that old negative drift cannot hide a new positive shift
why: Correct: without the floor, a long quiet period would build a debt that delays alarms.

questions.q: Scenario: you get too many false alarms from CUSUM. Which change helps?
why: Correct: a higher limit needs more evidence.

questions.q: Scenario: after a release the mean latency moves up by 5 ms, the standard deviation is 20 ms. Which tool is more likely to find it soon?
options: A z-score with limit 3 on each point
why: The shift is only 0.25 standard deviations; single points will rarely pass 3.
Correct: CUSUM adds the small excesses.
The maximum is dominated by noise.

questions.q: When does CUSUM give an alarm?
options: When S+ or S− is above h
When x is above the mean
why: That happens half of the time.
